fields.category: Jujube varieties recommended in USDA Farmers' Bulletin 2087

rows.name: Sui men
rows.description: Locke says Sui men begins to ripen slightly earlier than Li and Lang, is more highly flavored, and has fruit much like a date in shape and size

rows.name: Lang
rows.description: Locke says Lang has pear-shaped fruit smaller than Li, grew more rapidly than other jujube varieties at Woodward, and was probably the best first variety to plant

rows.name: Li
rows.description: Locke says Li has the largest fruit of the three listed jujube varieties, ripens last, and may yield more than other varieties in some localities, but can crack and mold in rainy ripening weather

fields.category: Persimmon varieties recommended in USDA Farmers' Bulletin 2087

rows.name: Early Golden
rows.description: Locke describes Early Golden as perhaps the best persimmon variety for the Southern Great Plains, larger than average native persimmons, ripening before frost, and having fine texture and good flavor

rows.name: Hicks
rows.description: Locke lists Hicks among the other good persimmon varieties for the Southern Great Plains

rows.name: Iona Market
rows.description: Locke lists Iona Market among the other good persimmon varieties for the Southern Great Plains

rows.name: Josephine
rows.description: Locke lists Josephine among the other good persimmon varieties for the Southern Great Plains

rows.name: Garretson
rows.description: Locke lists Garretson among the other good persimmon varieties for the Southern Great Plains

rows.name: Kawakami
rows.description: Locke describes Kawakami as a hybrid from northeastern Texas that proved hardy at Woodward, Oklahoma, but produced only light crops

fields.category: Grape varieties for eastern and southern Southern Great Plains

rows.name: Beacon
rows.description: Locke lists Beacon for the eastern and southern portions of the Southern Great Plains and describes it as a good-quality general-purpose grape for table and juice use

rows.name: Caco
rows.description: Locke lists Caco for the eastern and southern portions of the Southern Great Plains and says it was one of the leading varieties at Tucumcari, New Mexico

rows.name: Extra
rows.description: Locke lists Extra for the eastern and southern portions of the Southern Great Plains and describes it as apparently adapted to a wider range of conditions than any other variety listed

rows.name: Carman
rows.description: Locke lists Carman for the eastern and southern portions of the Southern Great Plains as a medium-sized black grape for table and juice use

rows.name: Ellen Scott
rows.description: Locke lists Ellen Scott for the eastern and southern portions of the Southern Great Plains and describes the fruit quality as excellent, especially on the drier western edge of the plains

rows.name: Armalaga
rows.description: Locke lists Armalaga for the eastern and southern portions of the Southern Great Plains as a high-quality green grape that is somewhat tender

rows.name: Edna
rows.description: Locke lists Edna for the eastern and southern portions of the Southern Great Plains and says it should probably substitute for Armalaga on the western edge of the plains

rows.name: Catawba
rows.description: Locke lists Catawba for the eastern and southern portions of the Southern Great Plains and says it was the only superior-quality grape showing promise as far north and west as Garden City, Kansas

rows.name: Last Rose
rows.description: Locke lists Last Rose for the eastern and southern portions of the Southern Great Plains as the latest maturing grape in the list

fields.category: Grape varieties for northwestern Southern Great Plains

rows.name: Alpha
rows.description: Locke suggests Alpha for trial in the northwestern Southern Great Plains, where many other grape varieties cannot be expected to succeed, and says it may be better adapted than Beta to heavy black soils

rows.name: Beta
rows.description: Locke suggests Beta for trial in the northwestern Southern Great Plains and says it made good yields at Woodward, Oklahoma

fields.category: Grape varieties not recommended for Southern Great Plains

rows.name: Concord
rows.description: Locke explicitly says Concord is not recommended for the Southern Great Plains because it is outside its territory, lacks drought resistance, ripens unevenly, and bears only light crops
